bib.title: AgentConductor: Topology Evolution for Multi-Agent Competition-Level Code Generation

legacy_report:
SOURCE: AgentConductor: Topology Evolution for Multi-Agent Competition-Level Code Generation. Siyu Wang, Ruotian Lu, Zhihao Yang, Yuchao Wang, Yanzhou Zhang, Lei Xu, Qimin Xu, Guojun Yin (Meituan), Cailian Chen, Xinping Guan (SJTU). Preprint arXiv:2602.17100v1 [cs.MA], 19-20 Feb 2026.

COVERAGE: All 21 pages read, 82021 of 82021 chars (main text, tables, appendices A-D). References were only skimmed. Note: the PDF has no ADAS (Hu et al.) entry. MaAS appears only as "Zhang et al., 2025", "Multi-agent architecture search via agentic supernet", listed with "Dang et al., 2025" (evolving orchestration) under "Dynamic orchestration methods". Neither is a baseline.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- claim: A 3B RL-trained orchestrator that emits per-query layered-DAG topologies in YAML beats all baselines on pass@1 across 5 benchmarks. APPS is the largest margin.
  number: APPS 58.8; LiveCodeBench v4 46.3; CodeContests 38.8; HumanEval 97.5; MBPP 95.1; margins over second best 14.6/3.1/1.1/1.0/0.7 points
  setup: Orchestrator is Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct. Worker agents run gpt-4o-mini. Metric is pass@1, mean over 3 runs, with a sandbox. Baselines are Vanilla GPT-4o-mini, AutoGen, MetaGPT, MapCoder, AFlow, FlowReasoner, Chain-of-Agents (32B), GPTSwarm, AgentPrune (complex and layered), MacNet (complex and layered) and G-Designer. Baselines use up to 20 agent nodes and the same roles and prompts.
  quote: "AgentConductor reaches pass@1 accuracies of 58.8%, 46.3%, and 38.8% on APPS, LiveCodeBench (v4), and CodeContests, respectively, outperforming the second-best methods by absolute margins of 14.6%, 3.1%, and 1.1% percentage points."
  where: p.7 (Table 2 on p.6)
- claim: The topology-optimization family (GPTSwarm, AgentPrune, MacNet, G-Designer) underperforms the fixed MetaGPT pipeline on average. The authors say MetaGPT is second best on average.
  number: Overall averages (Table 2): MetaGPT 68.7; MapCoder 66.6; FlowReasoner 67.5; Chain-of-Agents 67.9; GPTSwarm 64.8; AgentPrune(Layered) 66.0; MacNet(Layered) 64.1; G-Designer 63.7; AgentConductor 72.1; AFlow 57.7
  setup: Table 2, 5 datasets, GPT-4o-mini backbone for workers.
  quote: "topology optimization methods underperform, likely because their learned topologies remain comparatively rigid and struggle to adapt to the highly variable and complex nature of competitive programming tasks."
  where: App. B.1, p.13
- claim: Token cost and density improve alongside accuracy on APPS. The paper abstract says up to 13% density reduction and 68% token cost reduction.
  number: Prompt/completion tokens: AgentConductor 277600/79800 vs best baseline G-Designer 320550/139200 (prompt) and Chain-of-Agents 334650/134250. Worst case AFlow 531450/184800. Scomplex (higher = sparser): AC 5.2 vs 2.4-4.1.
  setup: APPS, Table 3. The token unit and the exact baseline behind "68%" are not defined.
  quote: "AgentConductor 58.8 277600 79800 5.2"
  where: Table 3, p.6; abstract "outperforming the strongest baseline by up to 14.6% in pass@1 accuracy, 13% in density reduction, and 68% in token cost reduction."
- claim: Density tracks difficulty. Easy problems get sparse graphs and hard ones get denser graphs. Competing methods show little or no density adaptation across difficulty. Hard per-turn node caps are 4/7/10 for easy/medium/hard.
  number: Nmax = 4, 7, 10 (per turn, 2 turns max, so up to 20 nodes)
  setup: Caps come from "statistical analysis of thousands of SFT-generated samples". Fig. 5 compares the 3 contest datasets by difficulty. The difficulty levels are the APPS tiers introductory, interview and competition.
  quote: "the per-turn upper bound under the three difficulty levels is set to 4, 7, and 10, respectively."
  where: p.5 (Eq. 12); Fig. 5 on p.8
- claim: The topology is a strict layered DAG. YAML "step" is a layer and "ref" is an edge. It allows within-layer parallelism and cross-layer references, with no edges inside a step. The authors argue chain, layered-adjacent-only, tree and mesh topologies each lack something.
  number: none
  setup: Roles are planner, searcher, algorithmer, coder, debugger, tester (the tester must be in the last step). Constraints are that first-step refs are empty and refs point only to earlier steps. Edges are intra-turn, inter-turn cross-agent, and inter-turn self-edges.
  quote: "chain topologies limit parallel interactions, layered topologies restrict communication primarily to adjacent layers, and tree topologies offer only local branching without flexible connections to earlier nodes."
  where: p.2 and App. C, p.16
- claim: Topology is regenerated within a single instance each turn from execution feedback, with at most 2 turns. Existing methods are described as frozen per problem or per dataset. Pruning methods reuse one graph per dataset, G-Designer generates per query but is static afterwards, and dynamic-orchestration methods (incl. MaAS) "finalize it before execution".
  number: K = 2 turns
  setup: The orchestrator sees (problem, history of prior graphs plus feedback). Early stop on PASSED.
  quote: "Dynamic orchestration methods(Zhang et al., 2025; Dang et al., 2025) select a topology through multi-round optimization but still finalize it before execution."
  where: Related Works 4.2, p.8; Alg. 1 in App. C.1
- claim: Density score formulas. Each term is normalized by the DAG's own size, so the score isn't a raw token count.
  number: Scomplex = exp(Snode + 2*Sedge + Sdepth). Snode = exp(-|V|/Nmax(l)); Sedge = exp(-|E|/(|V|(|V|-0.5))); Sdepth = 1 - s/|V|
  setup: Derived from a cost model C = m*(|V| + |V||V_prev| + 2|E|), with the depth term added for latency. Depth is set to the layer count s, using Theorem 1 (depth = number of parts b). Reward rg = Scomplex if |V| <= Nmax, else tanh((Nmax-|V|)/Nmax).
  quote: "Scomplex = exp(Snode + 2·S edge +S depth)"
  where: Eq. 6-7 p.4, Eq. 13 p.5, App. C.2
- claim: SFT is required, and every reward component matters.
  number: Without SFT, valid topologies 15% (APPS) and 13% (HumanEval). Without RL, APPS 29.8 with 56.5% valid. Without the YAML error reward, 30.3 / 56.8% valid. Without the code-error reward, 35.5. Without Snode, 49.2. Without Sedge, 45.5. Without Sdiameter, 48.3. Without rg, 52.6 with density worsened (Scomplex 3.0).
  setup: Ablation Table 4, full model 58.8 / 5.2 / 100% valid. Performance for "w/o SFT" is "–" (not reported).
  quote: "w/oRL 29.8 2.7 56.5 90.2 3.2 57.2"
  where: Table 4, p.7
- claim: Training details. SFT on 4,500 GPT-4o/4o-mini-generated YAML topologies, then GRPO. Rewards are listed per error type.
  number: 4,500 SFT examples (2,700 competition-level graphs plus 300 basic initial examples; 450 first-turn problems, 50 per tier per dataset); LoRA lr 1e-4, batch 4; GRPO G=8, batch 8, lr 1e-6, temp 1, max completion 4096 tokens; 4x A800 GPUs. Rewards: PASSED 1.5, WRONG ANSWER 1.0, TLE 0.9, MLE 0.8, RUNTIME ERROR 0.7, COMPILATION ERROR 0.6; YAML errors -2.0/-1.5/-1.0/-0.5.
  setup: Verl and vLLM, code adapted from Search-R1. The KL term is computed over topology tokens only.
  quote: "Combined with first-turn runs, this yielded 2,700 competition-level interaction graphs."
  where: Sec 2.2 p.4; Table 1 p.5; App. A.2 p.11
- claim: The frozen orchestrator transfers a little. Zero-shot on 50 filtered text-only GAIA samples, with 2 new roles added and no retraining, it scored 15.8%. After retraining with a binary answer reward on new roles, it beat Chain-of-Agents 7B on GAIA, HLE and PopQA.
  number: Zero-shot 15.8%. Table 5, AC 3B vs CoA 7B: GAIA avg 53.8 vs 50.8; HLE 22.6 vs 18.0; PopQA 50.3 vs 46.5
  setup: B.4 is zero-shot with no training. B.5 retrained on subsets of GAIA, HLE and PopQA with an LLM-based answer validator. Seeds: 3.
  quote: "the framework achieved a success rate of15.8%on the selected GAIA samples"
  where: App. B.4-B.5, p.15
- claim: Layered graphs fit code generation better than unstructured "complex" graphs. AgentPrune and MacNet do better with layered initialization.
  number: AgentPrune Layered avg 66.0 vs Complex 65.9. MacNet Layered 64.1 vs Complex 63.9. The gap is tiny and APPS is mixed (MacNet 36.9 vs 37.6).
  setup: Table 2.
  quote: "layered graphs provide a more suitable inductive bias than unstructured complex graphs."
  where: App. B.1, p.13

LIMITS
- Only one orchestrator size (3B) and one worker model (gpt-4o-mini). There is no stronger-orchestrator or different-worker study.
- Baselines are capped at 20 nodes "for fairness". Baselines were re-run under the authors' roles and prompts, so numbers may differ from the originals. The authors do not report each baseline's own tuning.
- Max 2 turns. The density caps (4/7/10) were chosen from the authors' own SFT data statistics, so the density reward is partly tied to GPT-4o's topologies.
- SFT labels come from GPT-4o with difficulty tiers. The topology dataset for training and evaluation overlaps in source (APPS, CodeContests, LiveCodeBench), so train/test separation is not stated clearly in the text.
- The appendix reads like a reviewer-response patch ("To address the reviewer's concern"), and a citation shows as "(?)" for Chain-of-Agents. The token cost reductions mention "up to", and the density metric is the authors' own, so it is self-defined.
- Zero-shot GAIA 15.8% on 50 samples is not compared against any baseline.
- No ADAS or MaAS is run as a baseline. MaAS is only named in related work (query-conditioned supernet, but topology fixed before execution).
- The Fig. 7/8 captions mislabel the RL curve (text says "first 110 RL training steps (Figure 8)", but the figure is 7). The ablation table label "Sdiameter" differs from Sdepth in the text.

BUILDS ON: GPTSwarm (Zhuge et al., 2024); AgentPrune "Cut the crap" (Zhang et al., 2024a); AgentDropout (Wang et al., 2025b); G-Designer (Zhang et al., 2024b); MacNet (Qian et al., 2024) for layered/complex/chain/tree topology types; AFlow (Zhang et al., 2024c); FlowReasoner (Gao et al., 2025) and Chain-of-Agents (Li et al., 2025) for end-to-end RL of workflows; MaAS agentic supernet (Zhang et al., 2025) and Evolving orchestration (Dang et al., 2025) as related; MapCoder (Islam et al., 2024) for the role pool; Search-R1 (Jin et al., 2025) for the RL code and retrieval; GRPO via Verl (Sheng et al., 2025); LLaMA-Factory (Zheng et al., 2024).

CODE: Orchestrator output format (Fig. 1, Fig. 6 prompt, Alg. 1). The YAML topology skeleton, verbatim from the extraction:
- step: 1
      agents:
           - agent:
               ref: []
Prompt rules (p.12): "The last step must include a `<tester>` referencing at least one of `<coder>` or `<debugger>`" and "In the first step, all agents must have empty `ref` fields." Algorithm 1 (p.17): per round, sample ok ~ pi(.|x,Hk); if no valid YAML, append the error and continue; G = DecodeTopo(ok); run each layer in parallel; the tester returns z_code; break on PASSED.

FIGURES
- Fig. 1 (p.1): YAML to graph mapping and two-turn evolution (planner/searcher/algorithmer/coder/tester/debugger). Shows how the YAML maps to a layered DAG.
- Fig. 2 (p.2): compares mesh, chain, tree, pruned and generated topologies versus AgentConductor (difficulty-specific density, per-task generation, feedback refinement). Best single picture for a topology-pattern taxonomy.
- Fig. 3 (p.3): three-stage pipeline (SFT, GRPO with reward, inference).
- Fig. 4 (p.6): cost vs density vs accuracy on APPS and a per-benchmark bar chart.
- Fig. 5 (p.8): Scomplex by difficulty for three datasets.
- Fig. 8 (p.14): case-study topologies per difficulty, including turn 2 adding agents after errors.

PROBLEMS: Text extraction is readable overall. Some tables run columns together (the numbers were checked against the printed rows). Fig. 1-3 text is jumbled, and the figures were not rendered, so figure content was inferred from captions and labels. The PDF contains no instructions aimed at the reader. "ADAS" does not appear at all, so nothing can be said about it from this source. One working file written outside the repo: /tmp/ac2.txt (scratch, not a report).
